This is scope-narrowing: the fixture is not the real tickets repository, the measurement is a threshold pass/fail rather than a before/after comparison of actual received bytes, and no child delivers an actual CI-run byte measurement of the real tickets branch. The 140 MiB synthetic blob exceeds the 102400 KiB limit on its own, whereas the real tickets branch pre-B6 has a different size profile; the threshold values chosen for the synthetic fixture may not reflect production behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a post-checkout step in the modified workflow that runs `git count-objects -v --no-promisor` and emits the size-pack line as a workflow annotation, then add a workflow integration test that checks the logged size-pack from a real checkout (or a faithful mirror of the tickets branch including its full history) against the baseline.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] B4 must add a grep/AST audit of all callers of `_blame_file_commits` in `src/` and assert each caller handles `None` explicitly, or document that `derive_caused_by` is the only caller.
evidence: B4 spec: '_blame_file_commits (blame.py:67-79) returns [] BOTH when the git call fails (if out is None: return []) AND when a successful blame yields no SHAs.'
B4 fix: 'This ticket must therefore FIRST change _blame_file_commits to return None on git failure and [] on a successful-but-empty result.'

B4 ACs cover only: (1) distinguishes None from [] at unit level, (2) derive_caused_by returns None on None-path, (3) empty-blame negative control, (4) no caused_by link written, (5) golden comparison with all paths succeeding. No AC says 'enumerate all callers of _blame_file_commits and confirm each handles None'.
The parent plan references blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513 as the only consumer path, but does not assert no other callers exist.
findings.finding: B4 changes the return contract of `_blame_file_commits` from returning `[]` on git failure to returning `None` on git failure. This is a breaking change to the function's public-within-module interface. B4's acceptance criteria audit only `derive_caused_by` as a consumer of this changed return value. No AC specifies that all callers of `_blame_file_commits` are enumerated and verified to handle `None` correctly. Any existing caller that tests `if not result:` or `for x in result:` will conflate `None` (failure) with `[]` (success-but-empty), potentially swallowing errors silently.
findings.location: child 42fa-676d-fbbb-4ac5, Acceptance Criteria and 'The code fix' section — missing caller audit for _blame_file_commits
scenarios: A second caller of _blame_file_commits in blame.py or an adjacent metrics module iterates the result directly; after B4, it receives None and raises TypeError at runtime on the first blobless blame failure.
A test for a different caller passes [] as a mock return value for the old failure case and None is never tested; the caller is silently broken in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'grep -n _blame_file_commits src/ returns exactly the definition site and one call site in derive_caused_by; no other caller exists.' Alternatively, rename the internal function to make the None-returning variant explicit (e.g., `_blame_file_commits_or_none`) and let the original wrapper remain for backward compat.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] B2 must enumerate all call sites of `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` in `src/` and either verify each handles the no-mount case gracefully or update each to check the return/state before proceeding.
evidence: B2 spec: 'Preserve ensure_store_mounted_best_effort as a non-raising best-effort API. It treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount and returns without error.'

B2 AC4: 'ensure_store_mounted_best_effort treats unreachable as do-not-auto-mount, returns without error, and never supplies force_new_store=True; the following strict path reuses the cached result and reports the actionable failure.' This covers only the 'following strict path' consumer pattern.
B2 files list includes src/rebar/_cli/_init.py and src/rebar/_lib_writes.py but does not enumerate all call sites of ensure_store_mounted_best_effort across the codebase.
No AC in B2 requires: 'grep -n ensure_store_mounted_best_effort src/ enumerates all call sites and each is verified to handle the no-mount-returned case.'
findings.finding: B2 changes `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort` to silently not mount the store (returning without error) when the remote is unreachable. This is a behavioral change to a function used by callers that may proceed to read from or write to the store without checking whether the mount succeeded. B2's behavioral wiring tests cover `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`, and `_create_tracker` but do not require an enumeration of all external callers of `ensure_store_mounted_best_effort`. A caller that silently receives no mount and then attempts a store read/write will produce a later, harder-to-diagnose error rather than the actionable failure message B2 aims to provide.
findings.location: child e879-2d83-e925-4f2b, Acceptance Criteria item 4 and 'Implementation plan' section ('ensure_store_mounted_best_effort as a non-raising best-effort API')
scenarios: A caller of ensure_store_mounted_best_effort in a different command (e.g., rebar comment, rebar transition) proceeds to call a store write after the function returns without mounting; it receives a cryptic 'store not initialized' error rather than the actionable remote-unreachable message.

After B2 lands, a new caller is added that reuses the old assumption (if the function returned, the store is mounted); the changed semantics are not surfaced by B2's tests because only the init code paths are tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'grep -n ensure_store_mounted_best_effort src/ is exhaustively reviewed; each call site either checks whether the store is mounted before proceeding or is in a context (such as the paired strict-init path) where the unreachable case is already handled by the cached probe result.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Expand the plan title (or add a prominent 'Also in scope' summary at the top) to name all six deliverable areas — clone cost, fail-closed fix, merge-driver prerequisite (B3), blame-abort correctness (B4), authorship resolver flags (B5), and stale-file deletion (B6) — so the title faithfully describes the full body of work.
evidence: Title: 'Cut tickets-store clone cost via CI partial clone + fail closed instead of bootstrapping an empty store'
Scope lists 6 children: B3 merge.ours.driver, B1 blob:none filter, B2 fail closed, B4 clone guidance + blame abort, B5 authorship resolver flags, B6 delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget
B5 ('add --no-renames and -c log.showSignature=false to the two authorship resolvers') has no connection to the title's two stated goals
B6 ('delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget') is a standalone cleanup task absent from the title
findings.finding: The plan title promises exactly two goals — cut clone cost via CI partial clone and fix fail-closed bootstrap — but the body delivers six children: B3 (add merge.ours.driver prerequisite), B4 (derive_caused_by blame-abort + guidance doc), B5 (authorship resolver git flags), and B6 (delete .bridge_state.bak-retarget) are all additional scope not mentioned or foreshadowed in the title. A reviewer or implementer scoping work from the title alone will miss roughly half the deliverables.
findings.location: Title vs. Scope section (children B3, B5, B6 especially)
scenarios: A reviewer approving the plan based on the title will not expect blame-abort changes or authorship resolver flag changes, potentially blocking or missing review of B4/B5
An implementer budgeting time from the title will underestimate scope by 3-4 children
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like: 'Cut tickets-store clone cost (CI partial clone), fix fail-closed bootstrap, harden blame/authorship resolvers, and delete stale .bridge_state.bak-retarget' — or restructure B5 and B6 into a separate housekeeping epic if they are not truly prerequisite to the clone-cost and fail-closed goals.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider whether future work following B4's pattern should split clone-guidance documentation from `derive_caused_by` behavioral changes into separate children, since each is independently valuable, testable, and releasable with distinct actors and change kinds.
evidence: 'B4 clone guidance doc + make derive_caused_by abort on any per-path blame failure' — structural 'and' joining a documentation artifact and a behavioral code fix
AC lines 7 and 4 address these two sub-concerns separately: 'The clone-guidance doc exists and states the measured numbers' vs. 'derive_caused_by returns None when blame fails on any path'
Different actors: the doc targets operators/CI authors choosing clone depth; the blame abort targets developers relying on correct caused_by attribution
Different change kinds: documentation vs. logic correctness fix in metrics/blame.py
findings.finding: Child B4 bundles two independently-releasable sub-concerns: (a) the clone-guidance documentation (a doc artifact for operators/CI authors stating measured numbers), and (b) a behavioral code change making `derive_caused_by` abort on any per-path blame failure (a correctness fix for developers). Each has its own AC, its own actor, and its own change kind; the doc could ship without the code change and vice versa. As scoped in the parent, B4 as a unit has more than one reason to change.
findings.location: Scope section, item 4: 'B4: clone guidance doc + make derive_caused_by abort on any per-path blame failure'
scenarios: The doc could be blocked by writing/review cycles while the blame abort (a P1-adjacent correctness fix) is ready to ship — bundling delays the code fix
A reviewer who approves the blame logic change may not be the right reviewer for the operational guidance document, creating review friction

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] B1's reconverge E2E test fixture must explicitly run `git config merge.ours.driver true` in the temporary repo (not relying on global config or workflow YAML), and must assert the absence of conflict markers in the merged result — mirroring B3's positive-control assertion.
evidence: B1 reconverge AC: 'Blobless tickets reconverge independent local/remote changes with the ours driver, retain expected events, and push the merge. Tier: real-Git E2E.'

B1 real-Git fixture section: 'Start git daemon on localhost … git worktree add uses unpack-trees … A real-Git E2E materializes tickets, creates independent local and remote changes, fetches/merges with the B3 ours driver, retains all expected events, and pushes successfully.' The phrase 'with the B3 ours driver' implies the driver is expected to be present but does not specify how it is configured in the fixture.

B3 AC3: 'A reconverge against a diverged remote in a fresh runner-shaped checkout resolves .bridge_state/* local-wins (not a text merge) and produces no conflict markers. Tier: integration in a real temporary git repo mimicking the runner setup.'
B3 AC4: 'The same scenario without the config produces the text-merge behaviour — the negative control proving the test detects the defect.'
B3's spec explicitly covers with/without the driver. B1 does not say it will set the driver in its fixture or rely on a shared fixture from B3.
findings.finding: B1's reconverge E2E AC ('Blobless tickets reconverge independent local/remote changes with the ours driver, retain expected events, and push the merge') requires that merge.ours.driver=true is configured in the test fixture's git environment. B1's test creates a temporary git repo mimicking a runner-shaped checkout. The driver configuration in production comes from B3's change to .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml — a YAML file that has no effect on a temporary git repo created in an integration test. B1's spec does not state that the test fixture will configure merge.ours.driver=true explicitly. If the fixture omits this, the test is either vacuously green (driver happens to be set in the test runner's global git config) or fails for the wrong reason (no driver, text merge, conflict markers). B3's own integration tests cover the with/without-driver reconverge scenario; B1 duplicates the scope without specifying fixture setup.
findings.location: child 037b-879e-fe13-47d2, Acceptance Criteria item 13 ('Blobless tickets reconverge … with the ours driver') and child 040e-3f0c-ae86-4212, Acceptance Criteria item 3 (reconverge integration test)
scenarios: B1's reconverge test runs without merge.ours.driver=true configured in the temporary git repo; the .bridge_state/* merge=ours attribute names an undefined driver; git silently falls back to a 3-way text merge; if the test only checks that events are retained and the push succeeds (not that no conflict markers appear), it passes vacuously while the actual driver behavior is untested.
The test runner's global git config happens to have merge.ours.driver=true from a previous test's setup; B1's test passes coincidentally and would fail in a clean environment.
findings.suggested_fix: In the B1 integration test that exercises the reconverge E2E, add `subprocess.run(['git', 'config', 'merge.ours.driver', 'true'], cwd=tickets_worktree, check=True)` before the merge step, and assert `'<<<<<<<' not in merged_content` to prove the ours driver resolved the conflict rather than producing conflict markers.
